audit.why: 50.37% Emerald+ over an early game Renekton owns outright and a late game Kassadin owns outright — the page's 'concede the lane, steal the game' framing is the right read. Renekton's kill window is levels 1-6 with Ruthless Predator up; Kassadin's is Rod of Ages onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[5] and win[6] were both labelled Renekton while their own captions say otherwise: whys[5] reads 'Catalyst/Rod of Ages stalling pulls you level with him' (that is Skill, not a Renekton win) and whys[6] reads 'your blink-stack assassination outscales his fully fallen-off early game' (that is a Kassadin win). full.phases[5]/[6] carried the same mismatch, with phases[6].why literally saying 'The monster is awake... Hunt.' under side Renekton.
audit.why: Renekton is the textbook early-game juggernaut who has no sustained threat after two items; Kassadin's Rod of Ages and Riftwalk-max spikes land exactly there. Nothing in either layer argues Renekton wins at 2+ items.
audit.corrected: First item to Skill, Two+ items to Kassadin, on both win[] and phases[].side. No why-text invented — the sides now match captions that were already written.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction in this matchup was missing and the pages asserted its opposite. Riot's Ruthless Predator text: 'If Renekton has more than 50 Fury, he slashes his target three times, destroying damage shields on the target, dealing high physical damage, and stunning them for 1.5 seconds.' It destroys your Null Sphere shield. Yet tradeGood, dosFull[0], dosFull[1] and breakdown.trading all told you to trade and 'walk out as the shield absorbs his counter', and dosFull[0].t said 'Hug XP range and absorb with Q shield'. Compounding it: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage only and Void Stone reduces magic damage only, while Renekton's damage is entirely physical — so content late's claim that 'your Void Stone magic-reduction and Q shield eat his shrinking burst' is wrong twice over.
audit.why: Two Riot descriptions settle it. Null Sphere: 'a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' Void Stone: 'takes reduced magic damage.' Renekton's Q, W and E are all physical, and the empowered W explicitly strips shields.
audit.corrected: The shield-strip is now the headline of the early game, spikes[0], whys[1], wants.foe[1], breakdown.cooldowns and Key Ability Interactions; the trade line now says his damage is physical so the Q shield stops none of it; the Void Stone claim in late is corrected to HP, armour and the blink.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Step up only on its downtime' with no number attached anywhere.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8s and Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s with two charges. Those two numbers are the entire step-up calculus.
audit.corrected: 16s-at-rank-1 down to 8s for W and the 16s Slice and Dice are now stated in mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds mention despite Cull the Meek being a heal that scales with Fury.
audit.why: Riot's Cull the Meek text: 'heals for a small portion of the damage dealt. If he has more than 50 Fury, his damage and heal are increased.' In extended trades that heal is what turns a lost all-in into a Renekton win, and Kassadin's AP build has a natural Grievous Wounds slot in Morellonomicon.
audit.corrected: wants.you[2] now names Morellonomicon after Rod of Ages so the full-fury heal stops paying his all-ins back.

audit.why: Null Sphere does not silence. Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels'.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the interrupt, which is the effect that actually exists.

edits.before: Renekton owns this completely and there is no trick that changes it — he is a point-and-click bully and you are at your weakest. Your only ability is Null Sphere, which gives a tiny 1.5s shield but costs a fortune in mana and won't survive his empowered W stun into a fury-stacked Q. Do not step up for a Q poke; he just W-stuns you and a full-fury Cull-the-Meek heals all of it back while you bleed mana. Last-hit at the very edge of Q range, accept the chip, and ping for jungle help if he has both Slice-and-Dice charges up to all-in you.
edits.after: Renekton owns this completely and there is no trick that changes it — he is a point-and-click bully and you are at your weakest. Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage only and Renekton is pure physical, so it does nothing here; worse, at 50+ Fury his Ruthless Predator (W) destroys damage shields on the target, eating the shield and stunning you 1.5s. Do not step up for a Q poke — he W-stuns you and a full-fury Cull the Meek heals it all back while you bleed mana. Last-hit at the edge of Q range and ping for jungle help when both Slice and Dice charges are up.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still survival — Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore on champion hits keeps your mana alive, but never auto him to proc it when his fury bar is full, because that's his strongest combo window. Level 6 is your lifeline, not a fight button: Riftwalk gives you a blink to dodge his E-in W-stun burst and to escape the ganks he sets up with his slow. Use it to disengage and farm under tower, not to chase — you do not out-damage a fury-stacked Renekton until you have items.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still survival — Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore on champion hits keeps your mana alive, but never auto him to proc it while his fury bar is full, because that is his strongest combo window. Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 and 8s maxed, so count it: the seconds after he spends it are the only ones you own. Level 6 is a lifeline, not a fight button — Riftwalk dodges his E-in W-stun burst and the ganks his slow sets up. Farm under tower with it; you do not out-damage a fury-stacked Renekton until items.

edits.before: This is the entire reason you suffered the lane. Now your escalating Riftwalk stacks let you blink onto him or his squishies repeatedly while your Void Stone magic-reduction and Q shield eat his shrinking burst. Don't grief it away early; just reach this window even and you flip the whole lane.
edits.after: This is the entire reason you suffered the lane. notes: full.diff is 'EVEN' while breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both say 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10' and tone is the red #ff5d6c. One of those is wrong; the 50.37% Emerald+ number supports EVEN overall with a hard lane phase. I left all four alone rather than guess which field the user wants moved. Also note the recurring kit-flag misfire: kassadin.json tags Null Sphere as a channel ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') and _missing-interactions.json builds a 'Renekton can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Ruthless Predator (W)' row on top of it. Riot's description says Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not one, so I did not write that row. The genuine Ruthless Predator interaction — shield destruction — is now on the page instead.
